The Nigerian Stock Exchange (NGX, officially Nigerian Exchange Group) is a leading integrated market infrastructure in Africa servicing the continent’s largest economy. The Exchange provides capital access to companies seeking to take advantage of the financial markets to fund their business expansion. Likewise, NGX provides its pool of domestic, regional, and international investors with an array of regulated securities to achieve their investment objectives. In March 2021, the erstwhile Nigerian Stock Exchange was demutualized from a member-owned not-for-profit entity into a shareholder-owned, profit making entity Nigerian Exchange Group Plc.

NGX publishes the benchmark, value-weighted All-Share Index (ASI), formulated in January 1984 with a base value of 100. The ASI tracks the general market movement of all listed equities on the Exchange, including those listed on the Growth Board, regardless of capitalization. Additional indices are the NGX30 and NGX50 which respectively track the top 30 and 50 companies in terms of market capitalization and liquidity. Both indices, in which only fully paid-up common shares are admitted, are weighted by adjusted market capitalization—the number of a company’s listed shares, multiplied by the closing price, and multiplied by a capping factor.

NGX TRADING SUMMARY FOR FRIDAY, JULY 3, 2026: At the end of the last weekday of trading on the Nigerian Stock Exchange (NGX), a total of 454,862,743 shares in 48,147 deals, corresponding to a market value of NGN 27,572,229,451.99, were traded. Compared with the previous NGX trading day (Thursday, July 2), today's data shows 47% decline in volume, 3% improvement in turnover, but 7% decline in deals. The current market capitalization of the Nigerian Stock Exchange is NGN 147.1 trillion (USD 107 billion).

In the aggregate, 133 NGX listed equities participated in trading, ending with 39 gainers and 14 losers. Airtel Africa led the gainers with 10% share price appreciation closing at NGN 5,274.00 per share, followed by The Initiates (+10%), Omatek Ventures (+10%) and Daar Communications (+10%). On the losing side, International Energy Insurance came out last with an end-of-day price depreciation of 9.96% at NGN 4.70 per share, followed by Meyer (-9.95%), Fortis Global Insurance (-9.8%) and Sovereign Trust Insurance (-5.34%). Zenith Bank recorded the highest volume of 49.8 million traded shares, followed by The Initiates (49.3m), Chams (28.4m) and United Bank for Africa (27.8m).

Regarding the performance of NGX market indices, the benchmark NGX All-Share Index (ASI) soared 4,918.37 (2.19%) points to close at 229,240.34, representing a 1-week loss of 1.21%, a 4-week loss of 5.36%, but an overall year-to-date gain of 47.31%. Other remarkable indices that performed were the NGX Top 30 Index (+2.26%; -1.09% 1WK; +46.67% YTD), NGX Banking Index (+2.78%; -3.72% 1WK; +35.31% YTD), NGX Pension Index (+2.52%; -2.1% 1WK; +55.41% YTD), NGX Main Board Index (+2.21%; +2.27% 1WK; +44.71% YTD), NGX Premium Index (+2.2%; -6.91% 1WK; +56.7% YTD), and NGX Insurance Index (+1.26%; -2.52% 1WK; -8.43% YTD).
